# Breadcrumb

Header: `winui/ui/navigation/Breadcrumb.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/navigation/Breadcrumb.hpp`.

A navigation trail (Home > Folder > File) of plain text items, root first.

Every item but the last is a small inline button that raises [on_item_click()](#on_item_click) with its index. The last is the current location. It is not clickable, has no trailing chevron and is never hovered or highlighted by the keyboard. The strip is one tab stop. Left/Right move a highlight among the clickable items, and Enter/Space activates it. The arrow keys alone never navigate. When the trail is wider than the control, the leading items fold into an ellipsis ("…"). Its flyout lists them nearest first, and picking one raises [on_item_click()](#on_item_click) with that item's own index.

The control never changes its own items. A click is a request, and the handler decides what to do, usually cutting the trail back to the clicked item.

Example: 
```cpp
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
ui::BreadcrumbControl* bar = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::BreadcrumbControl>(
    std::vector<std::string>{"Home", "Documents", "Design", "Northwind"}));
bar->on_item_click([bar](std::size_t index)
{
    std::vector<std::string> items = bar->items();
    items.resize(index + 1); // navigate up: drop everything after the clicked item
    bar->set_items(std::move(items));
});
window.set_content(std::move(stack));

// Declaratively, reporting the clicked folder:
ui::Property<std::string> location{"Design"};
ui::Control<ui::Breadcrumb> crumbs;
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .content = {
        ui::Breadcrumb{
            .items         = {"Home", "Documents", "Design"},
            .on_item_click = [&](std::size_t index) { location = crumbs->items()[index]; },
            .control       = crumbs,
        },
        ui::Text{.text = location},
    },
});
```

## `ui::Breadcrumb`

A navigation trail (Home > Folder > File). Builds a [ui::BreadcrumbControl](#uibreadcrumbcontrol). The last item is the current location and is plain text. Every earlier item fires [`.on_item_click`](#uibreadcrumb-on_item_click) when clicked or Enter/Space-activated.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::Breadcrumb> trail;

window.set_content(ui::Breadcrumb{
    .items         = {"Home", "Documents", "Design", "Northwind"},
    .on_item_click = [&](std::size_t index)
    {
        // Navigate up: drop everything after the clicked folder.
        std::vector<std::string> items = trail->items();
        items.resize(index + 1);
        trail->set_items(std::move(items));
    },
    .control = trail,
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Breadcrumb{
    .items, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height,
    .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility,
    .on_item_click, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uibreadcrumb-items"></span>`items` | `ui::Binding<std::vector<std::string>>` |  | The trail, root first; the last entry is the current location. Bind it to a property and assign a shorter trail to go back up. |
| <span id="uibreadcrumb-on_item_click"></span>`on_item_click` | `ui::Callback<void(std::size_t)>` |  | Called with the index of an activated item. Never fires for the last (current) item. |
| <span id="uibreadcrumb-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uibreadcrumb-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uibreadcrumb-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uibreadcrumb-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uibreadcrumb-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uibreadcrumb-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uibreadcrumb-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::Breadcrumb>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `enabled`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::BreadcrumbControl](#uibreadcrumbcontrol); the caller owns it.

### BreadcrumbControl

```cpp
BreadcrumbControl()
```

An empty trail; it draws nothing and is not focusable.

### BreadcrumbControl

```cpp
BreadcrumbControl(std::vector<std::string> items)
```

A trail of [`items`](#items), root first; the last is the current location.

### ~BreadcrumbControl

```cpp
~BreadcrumbControl() override
```

Destroys the ellipsis flyout with the control.

### BreadcrumbControl

```cpp
BreadcrumbControl(const BreadcrumbControl&) = delete
```

Non-copyable, like every [Element](../tree/element.md).

### operator=

```cpp
BreadcrumbControl& operator=(const BreadcrumbControl&) = delete
```

Non-copyable, like every [Element](../tree/element.md).

### items

```cpp
const std::vector<std::string>& items() const
```

The trail, root first (UTF-8); the last entry is the current location.

### set_items

```cpp
void set_items(std::vector<std::string> items)
```

Replaces the item list and clears the hover, press and keyboard highlight, closing an open flyout. Updates the layout. Safe to call from inside [on_item_click()](#on_item_click).

### on_item_click

```cpp
void on_item_click(Callback<void(std::size_t)> handler)
```

Fires with the index into [items()](#items) when a clickable item is activated by a click, Enter/Space, or from the ellipsis flyout. Every item but the last is clickable. Replaces any previous handler.

### ellipsis_shown

```cpp
bool ellipsis_shown() const
```

Whether the leading items are folded into the ellipsis because the trail did not fit its width, as of the last arrange.

### first_shown_item

```cpp
std::size_t first_shown_item() const
```

Index of the first item drawn after the ellipsis (0 when nothing is folded); items before it live in the flyout.

### item_bounds

```cpp
std::optional<Rect> item_bounds(std::size_t index) const
```

An item's rect in window coordinates as of the last arrange, or nullopt when it is folded into the ellipsis or `index` is out of range.

### ellipsis_bounds

```cpp
std::optional<Rect> ellipsis_bounds() const
```

The ellipsis item's rect while it shows; nullopt when nothing is folded.

### flyout_open

```cpp
bool flyout_open() const
```

Whether the ellipsis flyout listing the folded items is open.

### set_flyout_open

```cpp
void set_flyout_open(bool open)
```

Opens or closes the ellipsis flyout (a click on the ellipsis toggles it). Opening does nothing while no items are folded or the control is disabled.

### focused

```cpp
bool focused() const
```

Whether the strip holds keyboard focus.

### focusable

```cpp
bool focusable() const override
```

Focusable while the control is enabled and has a clickable item, which takes at least two items since the last one is never clickable.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

A Group: the items are plain strings with no automation nodes of their own.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

The whole trail's natural width (items, chevrons) and one row's height; it never wraps.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Decides how many leading items fold into the ellipsis so the rest fit `final_rect`.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the items, chevrons, the ellipsis and the keyboard focus ring. Hover and press change the text color, and in some themes the background.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

Button-style clicks: a press on an item followed by a release anywhere activates it. A click on the ellipsis toggles the flyout.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

Left/Right move the keyboard highlight and Enter/Space activates it. Up, Down and Escape work in the open flyout.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Called by [Window](../tree/window.md). Gaining focus puts the keyboard highlight on the ellipsis if it shows, else on the first shown clickable item. Losing focus clears the highlight. Redraws.

### focus_ring_rect

```cpp
Rect focus_ring_rect(const Theme& theme) const override
```

Around the focused item, or the ellipsis.
